summary: Rogue River NF emergency lookout: 40-ft pole L-5 built 1935 or 1936 near the Owen-Oregon CCC camp; later removed or destroyed; no current site description found.

facts.status_note: Register says the tower was later removed; firelookout.com says it was later destroyed. The Forest Fire Lookout Association list shows Tower Gone.

events.note: Oregon Forest Lookouts quotes a forest history entry: 40-ft round timber tower with a 10x10 house on an emergency lookout point near Camp Two.
Built at the site of the Owen-Oregon CCC Camp as a 40-ft pole L-5 tower (register and firelookout.com).
Five-man crew did maintenance at the emergency lookout near their camp; $100 allotted for repairs (forest history quoted by Oregon Forest Lookouts).
Registered November 24, 2010, nominated by Ray Kresek (US 775, OR 184).

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Oregon Forest Lookouts quotes a forest-history entry that dates the tower to 1935; the register and firelookout.com say 1936. The story gives both dates and does not choose.
The register says the tower was later removed; firelookout.com says later destroyed. The story reports both.

notes_for_editor: Four pages read; the record is thin. Build year is the open point (1935 forest-history entry vs 1936 register and firelookout.com). The Owen-Oregon CCC camp link comes from the register and firelookout.com only. Oregon Forest Lookouts also has a c.1950 line about a lookout on the north side of the old South Fork CCC camp; it does not name Camp Two, so it is left out. A web search snippet said no source mentioned Owen-Oregon CCC camp; the two pages read here do, so the snippet was wrong. No staffing, access, or current-site information found. Photos on firelookout.com credit the Fire Lookout Museum with no licence shown; none added. Brief had no design or height; both added from the register (40 ft, L-5).
